# antiRea

> antiRea is an evidence-led, server-side TypeScript toolkit that meters dataset access per identity and detects coordinated bot abuse - advisory signals, zero runtime dependencies, and nothing blocked by default.

## Overview

antiRea is for web apps and SaaS products in general - any service where an account can read, export or enumerate a dataset. It is not primarily a live-room tool; one signal family also covers shared live rooms and communities.

A normal web app is wide open to bulk extraction: in antiRea's tests, one account and a single export call walked away with an entire 10,000-record dataset in under 200 requests, quietly. With antiRea wired in, data is metered per record - one identity can only ever receive a capped slice (20 percent of the dataset in the test setup), so full extraction stops being an export call and becomes an identity problem. In the measured v2.5.0 classic round described in the project materials, the REA-style run that took one account unprotected was stopped at 5 percent of the dataset, and a scripted slicing crew that insisted on finishing needed 25 identities and about 19 minutes, flagged by the herd detector and the evidence engine on the way.

Everything is advisory: antiRea measures and reports, the host application decides, and legitimate users were measured at zero friction in the project materials (declared team 1,200/1,200, polite users zero consequences). It cannot prevent anyone from inspecting code delivered to their browser, and it does not stop a determined, well-resourced rebuilder.

## Install

- Runtime: Node 20+
- License: MIT
- Dependencies: zero runtime dependencies
- npm: npm i @dannyphan190/anti-rea
- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@dannyphan190/anti-rea
- Source: https://github.com/dankezo/antiRea
- Landing: https://antirea.dannyphan.me
- Current version: 2.8.0
- Tests: 812 automated tests (810 passing, 2 skipped)

## Key modules and capabilities (from canonical listing copy)

- Per-identity record budgets: meter dataset access per identity, per record
- Priced exports and session-chained cursors
- RFC 9421 Web Bot Auth signature verification for signed agents
- Canary traps
- Python/FastAPI quota-guard port
- Coordinated-cohort signal family (advisory, names nobody until a cohort confirms): herd phase, herd tightness, seat occupancy, activity phase, vote brigading, room hopping, reconnect storms
- createRoomGuard (new in 2.8.0): combines the room signal family with occupancy pressure laws into one guard that recommends step-up only for new joins
- Evidence layer (new in 2.8.0):
  - CS-02: config provenance hashes
  - BS-01: verified-neutral identity facts and Web Bot Auth verdict classification
  - CAP-01: single-use step-up proofs
  - KT-01: evidentiary roles for audit packs

Named entry points visible in the README include createRecordBudget, createQuotaGuard, createExportGuard, createExpressQuotaMiddleware, createWebBotAuthVerifier, createCanaryMaze, createHerdDetector, createRoomGuard, createConfigProvenance and createStepUpProofVerifier.

## MCP

antiRea also ships an MCP wrapper, @dannyphan190/anti-rea-mcp on npm, listed on the Official MCP Registry. It exposes the library's advisory signal evaluations as MCP tools so an AI agent can open a signal session, feed it events and read the verdict. Production integrations still import the library in-process.
